sections.overview: The crested lark ranges across Eurasia and North Africa; northern populations may migrate, while many others are resident.
sections.identification: This 18 cm brown streaked lark has a conspicuous pointed crest, broad wings and a short rounded tail.
sections.habitat: It favors warm open ground, including cereal fields, fallows, roadsides and suburban edges.
sections.diet: It eats invertebrates, seeds, leaves and shoots, with plant foods more important in winter.
sections.behavior: It often sings from the ground or a low perch and remains territorial during breeding; most Iberian populations are sedentary.
sections.reproduction: It nests in a lined ground depression, usually laying three to seven eggs; Spanish birds may raise two or three broods.
sections.ecology: It uses cultivated open country and resembles the closely related Thekla’s lark, Galerida theklae.
sections.conservation: It is globally Least Concern, although BirdLife reports European declines. In Spain, SEO links population decline to agricultural change.
